answer_1.quote: ...goal is to generate a summary for each review that highlights commonalities, differences, and unique perspectives, thereby distinguishing one review from others of the same submission...
datasets: ICLR peer review dataset (28062 reviews for 8428 submissions)
answer_1.outputs: Summaries of individual scholarly reviews (extractive or abstractive).

answer_2.quote: ...We evaluate the generated summaries using the SEAHORSE metrics trained on human judgment. They assess the summaries along six axes: coverage, attribution, comprehensibility, grammar, repetition and conciseness. ... We also report ROUGE scores ... and perplexity of candidate summaries...

answer_4.quote: ...Since the main goal of the D-MDS task is to highlight the most unique information from each review, we asked human evaluators to identify the source review for each summary (See Appendix A for details about the human evaluation task)...
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators were asked to read a generated summary and select which review it originated from, measuring discriminativeness and uniqueness.
